title: Dynamic Holdback and Throttle Policy — proposal
content:
Summary:

This is a working PRD sketch for a Dynamic Holdback + Throttle Policy layered on top of the existing Dedicated capacity model. The goal is to give product and SRE a single control that: (a) preserves latency SLOs for high-priority lanes under sudden demand spikes, (b) reduces noisy-neighbor impact, and (c) enables predictable, rentable burst options without wholesale overprovisioning.

Context and problem:
- Many tenants run bursty inference patterns (short queries, high concurrency) that create SLO tail risk for other tenants sharing Dedicated pools.
- Current strategies rely on static reservation margins or ad-hoc tenant throttles; these either waste capacity or cause hard failures when traffic patterns change.
- Sales wants a burst offering that can be priced and tracked (burst credits or on-demand burn), and SRE wants an operational model for graceful degradation.

Goals:
- Maintain 99th percentile latency targets for priority lanes 95% of the time during sudden demand spikes.
- Provide a dynamically sized holdback pool (0–20% of pool capacity) that adjusts to demand/forecast signals and tenant SLAs.
- Support per-tenant soft-throttle (rate/concurrency) and hard-eviction policies with audit logs and observability.
- Allow an opt-in burst pay mechanism tied to holdback usage (billing and chargeback).

Non-goals:
- Replacing full autoscaler — this augments autoscaling and pool orchestration.
- Solving model-architecture-specific inefficiencies (quantization, custom kernels).

Design overview (high-level):
1) Holdback pool controller
   - A controller owns an internal shard of capacity designated as the holdback. The holdback can be physical (reserved nodes) or logical (concurrency slots).
   - Size is computed continuously from a moving-window forecast, recent tail-latency incidents, and SLA weightings across tenants. Baseline formula (proto): holdback_pct = clamp( max(1%, forecasted_spike_pct * 1.1, tail_incident_factor*5%), 0, 20 ).

2) Multi-dimensional throttle policy
   - Dimensions: token_rate (tokens/sec), concurrency, and request_priority (lane).
   - Each tenant has a configurable policy bundle: {priority_class, baseline_rate_cap, burst_credit_bucket}. Policies are applied in request admission pipeline.

3) Burst credit mechanism
   - Tenants accrue small recurring credits (or buy credits) enabling them to consume holdback capacity for short bursts. Credits are time-decaying to discourage hoarding.
   - Overuse beyond credits triggers gradual rate limiting, then soft-degradation (lower-fidelity model variants or quantized variants), then worst-case hard throttle.

4) Fairness & preemption rules
   - Priority classes: gold/silver/bronze + internal-system. Higher classes can preempt lower classes in holdback allocation with transparent logging and billing notes.
   - Preemption is optionally gated by customer SLA windows (customer-configured maintenance windows cannot be preempted).

Operational flow (runtime):
- Incoming request hits admission: check baseline caps -> consult burst_credit_bucket -> consult holdback controller state -> allow/limit/reject.
- If holdback is consumed -> route lower-priority requests to fallback (hosted API or cheaper model variant) with a contextual header that explains degradation.

APIs/Config (user-facing and admin):
- Tenant config: priority_class (string), baseline_rate_limit (int tokens/sec), concurrency_limit (int), burst_credits_enabled (bool), max_burst_consumption_per_minute (int).
- Admin console/CLI: holdback_target_pct (float), forecasting_window_mins (int), tail_incident_multiplier (float), enable_preemption (bool).

Observability and billing hooks:
- Metrics: holdback_size, holdback_used, per-tenant_burst_consumption, preemptions_count, degrade_events, 99p_latency_by_lane.
- Logs: event entries for credit burn, preemption, holdback resize decisions with causal reason tag.
- Billing: daily snapshot of holdback usage for each tenant (used_credits -> invoice).

Ops playbook (short):
- When 99p latency rises above SLO: check holdback_used > 90%? If yes -> increase holdback target by +3% (manual or auto if enabled) and trigger warmup pipeline.
- If preemption rate high for >10m: pause auto-preemption, roll back holdback change, open incident.
- Recovery: throttle low-priority lanes and notify SEs.

Safety & failure modes:
- Overly aggressive autosize could starve throughput; clamp holdback changes and use cooldown periods (e.g., 10m).
- Billing surprises: ensure burst events are clearly surfaced in console and optional customer notifications.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Physical vs logical holdback: physical nodes are simpler to guarantee latency but less efficient. Logical slots are more flexible but harder to enforce for GPU memory pressure workloads.
- Credit pricing model: flat per-credit price vs dynamic time-of-day multipliers.
- How to integrate with Dedicated "burst to hosted" fallback in regulated/air-gapped private deployments? Need policy exceptions for private deployments.

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
- Spike: implement holdback controller simulator (SRE/Applied ML) to run historical traffic traces to evaluate hit rates and fairness (2 weeks).
- Proto: admission filter + credit bucket prototype behind a feature flag in staging (4–6 weeks).
- Pilot: roll out to 2 internal tenants and one external early access customer with billing toggled off (8–12 weeks).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a hybrid ops+billing surface — need product and finance alignment before releasing credits billing.
- Cross-reference: DED-413 (forecasting signals), and the autoscaler telemetry contract PR (GH #1289) which adds required metrics hooks.

TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Run simulator on last 6 months of production traces (assigned: Lena).
- [ ] Draft customer-facing FAQ for burst billing and preemption (assigned: Diego).
- [ ] Wire up preemption audit logs into Console trace view (assigned: Eng infra).

Rough back-of-envelope: if holdback averages 8% of pool and converts 2% of old overprovision into burstable capacity, expected cost saving ~7–10% across multi-tenant pools (tentative).

End of draft.

(Comments and scribbles welcome — please add inline where you see data gaps.)
